main_text.p: fex maximus, eū in tēplo absconditū in lucem & confpectū populi deducit, ungit in Regē & diademate, & regalibꝰ ornamentis induit;quo nuntio experrecta Athalia occurrit,viditq; populū circum-quaq; manibus plaudentem & canentē tubis, unde attonita scidit vestimenta sua,clamauitq; Coniuratio,Cōiuratio. Quis tulerit Gracchos, de seditione querentes? Certè non tulit Ioida, sed praecepit Centurionibus, ut educerent eam extra septa Templi, & quicunq; eam sequutus esset, gladio feriretur: impofuerunt q; ei manus,& impegerunt eam per viam introi- tus equorū iuxta palatiū Regis, & interfe-cta est ibi: sic fera venit, sed certa tamen vindicta Deorū, laneos fortassis habent pedes, sed plumbeas, imò ferreas man°[?].

Ioas autem, cum Hazael rex Syriæ iam instrueret exercitum, & copias educeret ad Hierosolymam expugnandam perterrefactus nimis, tulit omnia sanctificata quæ consecrauerat Iosaphat & Ioram & Ochosias Patres eius, reges Iudæ, & quæ ipse obtulerat, & vniuersum argentum quod inveniri potuit in thesauris Templi Domini, & in palatio Regis, misitq; Hazaeli

page.notes: The line "Quis tulerit ... querentes?" has a decorative italic Q; it is read as part of the same paragraph. The paragraph is treated as continuing from the previous page. The second half of the final line lies on the cut-off part of the page. The italic "q;" after "impofuerunt" is read as a stroked q and may need checking. Top line is a fragment cut off at the top of the scan. "man°" has a superscript sign that may be a contraction for manus; not certain. Italic and roman boundaries in the last sentence are read from the scan and may be slightly off. Right-hand edge of the page is cut and shows show-through; ignored.
